text.short: Elko, 460 Commercial Street. Bread all day, and on Thursday and Friday nights the only pintxo-pote in this directory — a pintxo and a pint for $5.
text.today: Deli hours are weekday mornings and lunch. Then twice a week the room turns into a bar: pintxos out on the counter, Basque cider on tap, and from 4:30 to 6 a pintxo with a pote — a pint of beer, a glass of house wine, or a glass of sagardoa — for $5 the pair. On Fridays you can watch or play mus.
text.history: Anamarie Lopategui started it on her own Basque side, with sandwiches. In December 2016 it moved into a restored historic building at 460 Commercial Street and grew a pintxo counter and a bar. Choch Goicoechea and Carolyn took it on in October 2022.
text.table: Basque chorizo on a French roll. A lamb sandwich. Pintxos on skewers. Imported sagardoa, patxaran, Basque wine, craft beer on tap.
text.note: Ogi is bread in Euskara. The name is the shortest statement of purpose in this directory.

x_kitchen.says: delicious, handcrafted Basque and American sandwiches, salads, pintxos (Basque tapas) and drinks — served in a beautifully restored historic building

seating.note: A counter and tables. On pintxo nights the counter is the point: you stand, you eat off a skewer, and on Fridays there is a card game going.

picon.note: The bar's own list names sagardoa, patxaran, Basque wine and craft beer on tap. It does not name a Picon.
